additions.reason: The compound concept 'the tzaddik when the world is gathered at him' is the active subject of the teaching. It is not simply 'the tzaddik' generically — the specific condition of having the world gathered is what defines this concept and what enables the bechina to Ish HaElohim and memshala. The Rebbe's proof (Elisha with his students = Ish HaElohim) confirms this: it is not Elisha alone but Elisha-with-students that IS Ish HaElohim. This node captures the combined tzaddik-plus-community reality that forms the Rebbe's subject. Not currently in the dataset for reference 166.

additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly uses 'נִקְרָא' for this contrasting state: 'כְּשֶׁהָיָה לְבַדּוֹ נִקְרָא אֱלִישָׁע סְתָם'. The 'סְתָם' (plain/simply/unqualified) is a conceptual marker — the word carries the meaning 'without further qualification, without the additional title.' It is not merely a narrative detail; it IS the name the Rebbe gives to the tzaddik-alone state. 'Elisha stam' is the bechina-name for the baseline condition, parallel to 'Ish HaElohim' as the bechina-name for the elevated condition. Not currently in the dataset for reference 166.

The contrasting state to 'the tzaddik when the world is gathered at him' (Package 1). The phrase 'כְּשֶׁהָיָה לְבַדּוֹ' (when he was alone) describes the tzaddik in solitude — this is the conceptual category that 'Elisha stam' names. The tzaddik alone IS 'plain Elisha'; they are bechina-equivalent. Not currently in the dataset for reference 166.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Elisha as a historical figure is referenced in the teaching, but the Rebbe's bechina statements attach to specific CONDITIONS of Elisha (with-students = Ish HaElohim; alone = Elisha stam), not to Elisha-the-prophet as a concept in his own right. The teaching is not about Elisha's general identity; it uses the two names as bechina-labels for two conditions. Adding 'Elisha' as a generic node would not capture the teaching's conceptual content and would conflate the two distinct states the Rebbe explicitly distinguishes. The meaningful conceptual nodes are the two named states ('Ish HaElohim' and 'Elisha stam'), not the underlying biographical figure.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: בְּנֵי הַנְּבִיאִים (sons of the prophets / students)
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The students/sons of the prophets are cited as the evidence case for 'הָעוֹלָם אֵצֶל הַצַּדִּיק' (the world gathered at the tzaddik). They are the demonstrating example, not a separate bechina concept. The Rebbe does not use 'נִקְרָא', 'הוּא בְּחִינַת', or any bechina formula for בְּנֵי הַנְּבִיאִים — they appear only as the narrative subjects of the Zohar citation. The conceptual category is 'הָעוֹלָם' (the world, the community that gathers), which is already captured in the compound node 'צַדִּיק כְּשֶׁהָעוֹלָם אֶצְלוֹ'. Excluded per framework rule: only concepts with explicit bechina language are added.

'הָעוֹלָם אֵצֶל הַצַּדִּיק' is the condition, not the bechina concept. The Rebbe does not say 'הָעוֹלָם הוּא בְּחִינַת X' — he says 'when the world is gathered, the tzaddik has memshala.' The world is the causal/conditional element (eitza side), not the bechina node. The bechina nodes are what the tzaddik IS in that state (Ish HaElohim, memshala). Excluded per framework rule: the causal condition is an eitza element, not a bechina node.
